tests.title: A repository is served at the organization and workspace path
given: a ready workspace in an organization and a valid owner credential
tests.when: a git client clones the external URL followed by /git/<org>/<slug>.git
then: the clone succeeds
the cloned refs match the workspace's repository
the path is built from the workspace's organization slug and its own slug
tests.pseudocode: in the git server integration test file: assert git_clone(url, cred).refs == store_refs(ws)

tests.title: A path without .git or with the wrong organization is not found
given: a ready workspace in an organization
tests.when: git requests are made without the .git suffix, with another organization's slug, and for a slug naming no workspace
then: each answers a pkt-line 404 ERR repository not found
the three answers are identical
tests.pseudocode: in the git server test file, table over the three paths asserting an identical pkt-line 404

tests.title: hub_url is the address actually served
given: a ready workspace with an organization, one without, and a service with and without an external URL
tests.when: each workspace is read and its hub_url cloned where it is not null
then: a non-null hub_url clones successfully
a workspace with no organization reports null and is served at no git URL
a service with no external URL reports null
tests.pseudocode: in the git server integration test file: u = read(ws).hub_url; assert (u is None) or git_clone(u).ok

tests.title: The Basic password is the credential and the username is ignored
given: an API key, a PAT with git scopes and an admin token
tests.when: a fetch is made with each credential as the Basic password, under several different usernames including an empty one
then: each credential is accepted whatever the username
all three kinds are admitted on a route their access allows
tests.pseudocode: in the git auth test file, table over (credential, username) asserting admission

tests.title: A missing, invalid or blocked credential is refused alike
given: no credential, a malformed one, a revoked one and a live one whose user is blocked
tests.when: a fetch is attempted with each
then: each answers 401 with a pkt-line error
the message does not say which condition applied
tests.pseudocode: in the git auth test file, table over the four cases asserting an identical 401 pkt-line

tests.title: Every git refusal is well-formed pkt-line
given: refusals for no credential, a member's push, a stranger, a bad service parameter and a failed lookup
tests.when: each is produced
then: each body parses as pkt-line
no body is a JSON error envelope
a real git client prints each message
tests.pseudocode: in the git auth test file, table over the refusals asserting parse_pktline(body) succeeds and body does not start with '{'

tests.title: A store token is neither accepted from nor disclosed to a client
given: a repo-scoped store token minted for a relay
tests.when: it is offered as the Basic password, and a successful fetch and a refused push are inspected
then: the offered store token is refused like any unknown credential
no response body or header of either request contains a store token
tests.pseudocode: in the git auth test file: assert fetch(basic=storeToken).status == 401; assert STORE_TOKEN not in response.text and not in headers

tests.title: Owner, admin token and member all fetch; owner and admin token also push
given: a ready workspace, its owner, an admin token and a member of its organization
tests.when: each fetches, and the owner and the admin token each push a branch
then: all three fetches return the same pack
both pushes are applied
the member's fetch result is identical to the owner's
tests.pseudocode: in the git access integration test file: assert pack(owner) == pack(member) == pack(admin); assert push(owner).ok and push(admin).ok

tests.title: A member's push and receive advertisement are refused
given: a member of the workspace's organization, holding a PAT with git:write
tests.when: the member requests the receive-service advertisement and then pushes
then: both answer a pkt-line 403 ERR org members have read-only access to this workspace
the repository is unchanged
the PAT's git:write does not help
tests.pseudocode: in the git access test file: assert advert(member, 'git-receive-pack').pkt == MEMBER_MSG and push(member).pkt == MEMBER_MSG

tests.title: A stranger and a foreign bound token are told the repository is not found
given: a stranger, a token bound to another workspace, an existing workspace, an archived one and a slug naming nothing
tests.when: each makes a fetch and a push against each workspace
then: every answer is a pkt-line 404 ERR repository not found
the answers are identical across the three workspace cases
tests.pseudocode: in the git access test file, table over (caller, workspace, operation) asserting an identical 404

tests.title: The git checks run in the documented order
given: a workspace whose repository is not ready, a member holding a PAT without git scopes, and a mismatched organization in the URL
tests.when: each combination is requested
then: the organization mismatch answers repository not found before readiness is considered
the unready repository answers ERR repository not available before access
a member's push is refused as a member before the PAT's scopes are considered
tests.pseudocode: in the git access test file, table over (urlOrg, repoReady, caller, patScopes, expectedMessage)

tests.title: A failed access lookup refuses the git request
given: a store whose membership lookup raises
tests.when: the owner, a member and a stranger each fetch and push
then: every request answers a pkt-line 500
no pack is served and no ref is updated
tests.pseudocode: in the git access test file: with lookup raising, assert every request's pkt-line is a 500 and refs() unchanged

tests.title: The git scopes gate fetch and push
given: PATs holding git:read alone, git:write alone, and neither
tests.when: each fetches and pushes
then: git:read fetches and is refused a push
git:write fetches and pushes
the PAT with neither is refused both with a pkt-line 403
tests.pseudocode: in the git access test file, table over (scopes, operation, expected)

tests.title: The ref advertisement is served for both services
given: a ready workspace and a credential with write access
tests.when: the advertisement is requested for the upload and the receive service
then: each answers 200 with Content-Type application/x-<service>-advertisement
a real git client parses each body
the advertised refs match the repository's
tests.pseudocode: in the git server integration test file, table over the two services asserting status, content type and parseability

tests.title: A missing or invalid service parameter is refused
given: a ready workspace and a valid credential
tests.when: the advertisement is requested with no service, an empty service and an unknown service
then: each answers a pkt-line 403 ERR invalid or missing service parameter
tests.pseudocode: in the git server test file, table over the three cases

tests.title: An incremental fetch transfers only what the client lacks
given: a repository with substantial history, and a client that has cloned it
tests.when: one commit is added and the client fetches again
then: the second fetch transfers far fewer bytes than the clone
the client ends with the same refs as a fresh clone would give
the negotiation exchanged have and want lines
tests.pseudocode: in the git server integration test file: b1 = clone_bytes(); add_commit(); b2 = fetch_bytes(); assert b2 < b1 / 10 and refs(client) == refs(store)

tests.title: Both protocol versions and a gzip body are served
given: a ready workspace
tests.when: a client clones asking for protocol v2, another asking for v0, and one sends a gzip-encoded request body
then: all three succeed
the resulting refs are identical in each case
tests.pseudocode: in the git server integration test file, table over (protocolVersion, contentEncoding) asserting a successful clone

tests.title: An accepted push is applied and reported
given: a ready workspace and a caller with write access
tests.when: a new branch, an update to an existing branch and a tag are pushed
then: the response is 200 with Content-Type application/x-git-receive-pack-result
each ref is reported ok
each ref is readable at its new value afterwards
tests.pseudocode: in the git push integration test file: r = push(refs); assert all(s == 'ok' for s in r.perRef.values()) and store_refs() == expected

tests.title: Exactly the refs reported ok are the refs that changed
given: a workspace and a push mixing refs that will be accepted and refs that will be refused
tests.when: the push is made and the repository's refs are compared before and after
then: the set of refs whose value changed equals the set reported ok
no ref reported ng changed
no ref absent from the report changed
tests.pseudocode: in the git push integration test file: before = refs(); r = push(mixed); assert changed(before, refs()) == {k for k,v in r.perRef.items() if v == 'ok'}

tests.title: A push refused outright changes nothing
given: a workspace with a known ref list
tests.when: a push is refused for a missing credential, for a member, for a stranger and for a missing git scope
then: every ref holds its previous value after each refusal
no object reached the store
tests.pseudocode: in the git push test file, table over the refusals asserting refs() == before and store.writes == 0

tests.title: A patch branch is refused when it is synced from the fork
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false, and a registered patch branch
tests.when: an update and then a deletion of that branch are pushed
then: the update is reported ng with "branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead"
the deletion is reported ng with the delete-on-the-fork message
the git_url in the message carries no userinfo
the ref keeps its old value
tests.pseudocode: in the push control integration test file: assert ng_message(push(update)) startswith 'branch is synced from origin; push to'

tests.title: A patch branch is forwarded to the fork and accepted only if the fork accepts
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin true, a fork that accepts one branch and refuses another, and a workspace with no usable fork credential
tests.when: updates are pushed for each case, and a deletion is pushed
then: the accepted branch is reported ok and holds its new value
the refused branch is reported ng with "origin rejected push: <error>" and keeps its old value
the workspace with no credential is reported ng naming the failure to resolve credentials
the deletion is refused as under the previous setting
the forward was not forced
tests.pseudocode: in the push control integration test file, table over the four cases asserting the per-ref report and the fork's received request

tests.title: A patch branch is accepted and then mirrored, and a failed mirror does not fail the push
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin true, and a fork that accepts, then one that refuses
tests.when: an update of a registered patch branch is pushed against each
then: both are reported ok and hold the new value
the fork that accepts received a forced push
the failed mirror leaves the push successful
tests.pseudocode: in the push control integration test file: assert push(update).perRef[ref] == 'ok' in both cases and fork.received.forced is True

tests.title: Ordinary updates are accepted with no push control
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin false, a standard workspace, and a carry_patch workspace receiving a branch that is not a registered patch
tests.when: an update is pushed in each case
then: each is reported ok and holds the new value
no request was made to the fork in any of them
tests.pseudocode: in the push control integration test file, table over the three cases asserting ok and fork.requests == 0

tests.title: Push control decides each ref of one push independently
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false
tests.when: one push carries a registered patch branch, an ordinary branch and a tag
then: the ordinary branch and the tag are reported ok and hold their new values
the patch branch is reported ng
the outcome of one ref did not change the outcome of another
tests.pseudocode: in the push control integration test file: r = push([patch, ordinary, tag]); assert r.perRef == {'patch':'ng','ordinary':'ok','tag':'ok'}

tests.title: A push to the protected namespace is rejected per ref while the push itself succeeds
given: a workspace holding a ref under refs/hub/replaced/
tests.when: a push carries a create, an update and a delete of refs under that namespace, alongside an ordinary branch
then: the push reports unpack ok
each protected ref is reported ng with the fixed message
each protected ref keeps its old value or stays absent
the ordinary branch is applied
tests.pseudocode: in the protected namespace integration test file: r = push(mixed); assert r.unpack == 'ok' and all(v.startswith('ng') for v in protected) and r.perRef['ordinary'] == 'ok'

tests.title: The protection holds for every workspace and every credential
given: a standard workspace and a carry_patch workspace
an API key, a PAT with git:write and an admin token
tests.when: a push to the protected namespace is attempted in each combination
then: every attempt is refused with the same message
no credential, the admin token included, can write the namespace
tests.pseudocode: in the protected namespace test file, table over (workspaceMode, credential) asserting an identical ng message

tests.title: Replaced refs are readable where the store accepts the namespace
given: a workspace with a ref under refs/hub/replaced/, against a store that accepts the namespace and one that does not
tests.when: the refs are listed remotely and the ref is fetched
then: where the store accepts the namespace the ref is listed and fetched successfully
where it does not, the read is unavailable and the push refusal still holds
the behaviour follows the store's capability report rather than a guess
tests.pseudocode: in the protected namespace integration test file, table over the two store capabilities asserting the read outcome and the unchanged push refusal

tests.title: head_sha is refreshed after every push
given: a ready workspace
tests.when: a push that is fully accepted, one partly refused and one whose every ref is refused are each made
then: after each, the workspace's head_sha equals the repository's HEAD
the refresh happens even when no ref was accepted
tests.pseudocode: in the git push integration test file, table over the three pushes asserting read(ws).head_sha == store_head(ws)

tests.title: A refused ref has no effect beyond the head_sha refresh
given: a carry_patch workspace with push control refusing a patch branch, and a recording fork
tests.when: a push carrying only that refused ref is made
then: no forward and no mirror request reached the fork
no field of the workspace record changed except head_sha
the ref keeps its old value
tests.pseudocode: in the git push test file: before = record(ws); push(refused); assert fork.requests == 0 and diff(record(ws), before) <= {'head_sha'}

tests.title: An agent clones and pushes against a running deployment with a real git client
given: a running deployment, a ready workspace and the afc credential helper configured
tests.when: git clone, a commit and git push are run against the workspace's hub_url
then: the clone succeeds and the working tree matches the repository
the push is accepted and the branch is readable afterwards
the workspace's head_sha is refreshed
tests.pseudocode: in the git server smoke test file: run('git clone', hub_url); commit(); run('git push'); assert branch in remote_refs() and read(ws).head_sha == tip

tests.title: A member clones and is refused a push, against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a workspace and a member of its organization with their own credential
tests.when: the member runs git clone and then git push
then: the clone succeeds and yields the same refs as the owner's clone
the push fails and git prints the member message
the repository is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the git server smoke test file: assert clone(member).ok; r = push(member); assert 'read-only access' in r.stderr

tests.title: One push, two refs, two outcomes against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false
tests.when: a real git client pushes a registered patch branch and an ordinary branch in one invocation
then: git reports the ordinary branch accepted and the patch branch rejected
the rejection message names where to push instead
the ordinary branch is readable afterwards and the patch branch is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the git server smoke test file: r = run('git push origin patch ordinary'); assert 'rejected' in r.stderr and ordinary in remote_refs()

tests.title: A push to the protected namespace is rejected while the rest lands
given: a running deployment and a workspace whose owner holds a live credential
tests.when: a real git client pushes a ref under refs/hub/replaced/ together with an ordinary branch
then: git reports the protected ref rejected with the hub's message
git reports the ordinary branch accepted
the protected ref still holds its old value
tests.pseudocode: in the git server smoke test file: r = run('git push origin HEAD:refs/hub/replaced/x HEAD:ordinary'); assert 'maintained by the hub' in r.stderr
